title: ochre-ware-retail-pilot-handoff-scratchpad
content:
TL;DR:
Quick capture from final pilot handoff call with OchreWare (small-format retail kiosks). Customer is ready to move from PoC to a 10-location pilot. Primary ask: on-device inference is not possible; they want a private Redwood deployment in a co-lo colocation with constrained egress and bursty connectivity. Key constraints = 150ms median inference target for 512-token flows, token cost sensitivity, and strict PII redaction requirements for customer SKUs and loyalty numbers.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (Redwood SE)
- Ravi Patel (Redwood Solutions)
- Sofia Martinez (OchreWare PM)
- Jonah Li (OchreWare SRE)
- Claire Nguyen (OchreWare Ops via recording)

Problem statement / customer goal:
- Replace rule-based receipt parsing + search with an LLM-powered assistant at kiosk checkouts and returns desk.
- Provide concise extraction (items, totals, loyalty id), confidence score, and match fuzzy SKU to internal catalog (embedding-based).
- Keep PII off-host (masking/redaction before logs leave their network).

Call notes (raw):
- Jonah: colocation has limited outbound bandwidth (1Gb shared) and infrequent site patch windows.
- Sofia: average receipt length ~120 tokens, but some vendor receipts hit 900 tokens (promo-heavy). We should handle tail.
- Claire: ops want on-call runbook for model fallback (e.g., if latency >350ms or storage full).
- Ravi: recommend two-tier model: a smaller quantized extractor for latency-critical inline parsing, and a higher-quality hosted model for post-facto enrichment during low-load windows.
- Security: OchreWare legal needs KMS + audit log proof that customer data never leaves their VPC unmasked.

Technical constraints and implications:
- Private deployment in customer VPC or co-lo with direct network peering. No public internet for inference endpoints.
- Autoscaling must be conservative (burst windows), prefer pre-warmed Dedicated pods for morning rush hours.
- KV cache warm start matters: first 50 requests each morning have higher latency. Consider a scripted warmup run.
- Tokenization mismatch risk: their POS system has OCR artifacts (garbled unicode) that inflate token counts — need tokenizer-aware preprocessing.

Requirements (explicit):
- SLO: 150ms median and 300ms p95 for parse endpoint under nominal load (<= 50 req/s across cluster).
- Data handling: redact loyalty numbers and 2 identified PII fields in-transit; persist only redacted text in logs.
- Rollout: start with 3 stores (canary) for 3 weeks, then scale to 10.
- Monitoring: per-request token breakdown and token-cost tagging; dashboard with false extraction rate per vendor.

Design suggestions (ideas to discuss in follow-ups):
- Model pair: llamav2-7b-qlo (quantized) for inline; llama-mini-13b-hosted for nightly enrichment (note: placeholder names).
- Use prefix-KV cache for identical vendor receipts (many stores use same receipt template). Cache key = (vendor-id + top-3 line fingerprint).
- Pre-filter step: quick regex extraction for obvious fields (dates, totals) to reduce model token load.
- Masking: client-side SDK in kiosk app performs deterministic redaction before sending. Keep SDK under Apache-2 license for easy audit.

Gotchas / Risks (action items tied below):
- OCR garbage -> token overage and cost spikes. Mitigation: add OCR cleanup script in kiosk (remove control chars, normalize whitespace) and a token estimator on edge to reject super-long inputs with a shortened pipeline.
- Cold KV caches after weekly maintenance windows. Warmup script + scheduled synthetic requests pre-opening.
- Legal may ask for model weights review for private deploy; prepare model-variant whitelist and license table.
- Backfill enrichment can leak raw receipts if operator forgets to enable masking. Need automation to enforce masked logs at ingestion pipeline.

Sample quick prompt (inline extractor) — for devs to test locally:
"""
System: You are a structured extractor. Extract: vendor, date (YYYY-MM-DD), items (name, price), total, loyalty_id (digits only)
User: <REDACTED RECEIPT TEXT>
Instructions: If loyalty id present, return masked value with only last 2 digits (e.g., ****34). If not present, return loyalty_id: null. Output JSON only.
"""
(We will run through Redwood's structured-output feature / function-calling in canary.)

Operational runbook notes (bullet):
- If p95 latency > 350ms for 5 consecutive minutes -> route to fallback model with lower compute (config change via route policy).
- If token cost > budget_threshold for 2 hours -> enable template regex extraction and limit model to enrichment-only on new receipts.
- If failed requests spike > 1% -> escalate to Jonah and Maya, gather logs (redacted).

Immediate next steps (owner / due):
- Maya: produce minimal pilot spec doc with compute estimate (gpus needed, qps headroom) — due 2025-11-12.
- Ravi: sketch autoscaling + warmup policy for morning burst (draft config) — due 2025-11-10.
- Jonah: confirm colocation networking constraints and provide PBX window for maintenance each week — due 2025-11-14.
- Sofia: share vendor receipt sample set (anonymized) + top-10 vendor templates — due 2025-11-09 (received via Slack).
- Legal (Claire): send redaction acceptance criteria and KMS requirements doc — due 2025-11-18.

Open questions (to confirm):
- Can we get an ops VM for warmup synthetic traffic, or do we need to schedule within their production hosts?
- Are there regulatory retention limits on redacted receipts per store/region?
- Do they prefer function-calling vs. structured-output enforcement for validation? (affects SDK).

Notes-to-self / dev hints:
- Prototype test harness: run a small Python script that hits /v1/parse with different token-length receipts and measures p50/p95. Capture token breakdown header.
- Use Redwood Optimize recommendations: start with quantization level q4_0 for the inline extractor; measure accuracy delta on their sample set before q3.
- Add a lightweight embedding index per store (faiss on NVMe) for SKU fuzzy match to reduce cross-store noise.

Meeting record links / artifacts:
- Slack convo: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C12345/p1630000000123456
- Recording: https://zoom.us/rec/share/ochreware-pilot-2025-11-05
- Linear: REDW-4321 (pilot: ochreware retail small pilot)

Scratch checklist (quick):
[ ] confirm model whitelist + licenses
[ ] finalize warmup script and schedule
[ ] produce per-store token cost estimate
[ ] craft simple SDK redaction snippet for kiosk team

Narrative note: keep this doc live during the handoff week. Most of this is rough; will consolidate into the pilot-spec doc once compute numbers are nailed down.

-- Maya
